## What does robusta instant coffee mean for an Indian kitchen?

### A plain definition

## How do you read the chicory line on the jar?

Ever notice the tiny text on the side of an instant coffee jar and wonder what it actually means? If you’ve ever stared at a label wondering if that fine print is hiding something, you’re not alone. Let’s look at the chicory line honestly. Purity Beans keeps it straight: the pure coffee jars — Purista and Purica — have 0% chicory. That means the jar is filled with nothing but coffee. It’s not trying to be something it isn’t. If you’re looking to avoid chicory entirely, reach for the jars marked zero. And a quick note on Prima: that one is a premium agglomerate made from pure Arabica, but it isn’t freeze-dried like the others. It sits on the shelf, but it’s not the one we’re talking about here. If you want to try the freeze-dried Robusta experience, the 50g jar of Purista is ₹319, and the 100g is ₹509. Both give you that bold, smooth cup without any added filler. Save the higher-caffeine kick for the Arabica blend, and you’ve got a clear path to the cup you actually want.

## Which jar suits the way you drink coffee?

Which jar suits the way you drink coffee? If you love a rich, syrupy black that cuts through the morning fog, the bold ground roast in the Bold jar is your partner—it's pure coffee, agglomerated for that deep, full-bodied kick. For someone who prefers a smoother, more nuanced cup with natural caramel notes, the Purica Arabica granule gives you that café-style lift without the bitterness. And if you are the kind of drinker who reaches for milk first thing, the Purista Robusta granule holds its own with a bold yet smooth body that doesn't get lost in the foam. Each style answers a different ritual, and the jar you keep on your counter says a lot about your morning. Stick to the 50g or 100g sizes listed on the site, and you’ll always know exactly what you’re getting. No hidden fillers, no mystery blends, just the honest coffee you asked for.

Both sizes are pure coffee, zero chicory, and perfect for an afternoon pick-me-up or as a gift for someone who appreciates a smooth, bold cup. I keep a jar at my desk because it dissolves instantly in hot water and never leaves any gritty residue. It is the kind of coffee that makes a regular morning feel a little more special, without the cafe price tag. ## How do people brew instant coffee in Indian cities?

Most people in Mumbai or Bengaluru don't have a grinder or a waiting line at a cafe. They reach for the jar. A spoonful, hot water, maybe a splash of milk—that is the rhythm of the day. Instant coffee lives in the pantry because it fits the schedule, not because it fits every connoisseur's ritual. Purista stands out because it is freeze-dried Robusta. That process locks in aroma in a way the standard agglomerated jars do not, giving a smoother cup without the bitter edge some instant brands have. ## How do you choose a jar without a slogan?

Choosing coffee from a shelf can feel like reading a foreign language, especially when every jar screams for attention with promises you did not ask for. Start by ignoring the front-of-the-box slogans and turn the jar over — the ingredient list is where the truth lives. If you see 'chicory' listed, put it back; that is the easiest way to avoid fillers. Look for the process, too: freeze-dried usually means a smoother cup, while agglomerated tends to be stronger and more budget-friendly. For a robusta lover, Purista offers that bold, smooth profile without any chicory mixed in. If you are curious about the difference between processes, remember that Purica is the freeze-dried Arabica option, while Bold sits on the agglomerated side.
